question: What does NDCC 43-23-06.1 define a "designated broker" as?
choice_a: A licensee designated by a real estate brokerage firm to act on behalf of the brokerage firm
choice_b: Any broker who supervises at least five salespersons
choice_c: A broker who has passed both the state and national portions of the licensing exam
choice_d: A broker who has held a license for at least two years
explanation: NDCC 43-23-06.1(5) defines "designated broker" as "a licensee designated by a real estate brokerage firm to act on behalf of the brokerage firm." Choices B, C, and D describe requirements or facts not found in this statutory definition.

question: Under North Dakota law, what distinguishes a "broker associate" from a firm's "designated broker"?
choice_a: A broker associate has not yet passed the state portion of the licensing exam
choice_b: A broker associate holds an active real estate broker's license but works under another broker or firm rather than acting as the firm's designated broker
choice_c: A broker associate is a salesperson who has completed continuing education but not broker prelicensing
choice_d: A broker associate may only handle commercial transactions, while a designated broker handles residential
explanation: NDCC 43-23-05.1 and 43-23-06.1 treat "salesperson," "broker," and "broker associate" as three distinct categories of licensee. A broker associate holds a full broker's license, having met the same education, experience, and examination standards as any broker, but chooses to affiliate with and work under a firm's designated broker rather than acting as that designated broker. B mischaracterizes a broker associate as unlicensed at the broker level; C wrongly conflates the tier with a salesperson; D invents a distinction not found in North Dakota law.

question: NDCC 43-23-06.1(7) defines "licensee" to include which three categories of persons associated with a real estate brokerage firm?
choice_a: A real estate broker, a title agent, and a real estate salesperson
choice_b: A designated broker, an appraiser, and a real estate salesperson
choice_c: A real estate broker, an associate real estate broker, and a real estate salesperson
choice_d: A real estate broker, an escrow officer, and a real estate salesperson
explanation: This is the exact statutory text of NDCC 43-23-06.1(7): a "licensee" is "a real estate broker, an associate real estate broker, or a real estate salesperson who is associated with a real estate brokerage firm." The other choices substitute unrelated occupations (title agent, appraiser, escrow officer) that are not "licensees" under this chapter.

question: Under NDCC 43-23-05.1, an organization formed by a licensed salesperson, broker, or broker associate may be licensed by the commission only if certain conditions are met. Which of the following is one of those conditions?
choice_a: The organization must employ at least one unlicensed assistant
choice_b: The organization must be owned by a licensed attorney
choice_c: The organization must maintain its own separate trust account independent of the supervising broker
choice_d: The organization must not advertise or portray itself to the public as a real estate broker or brokerage firm
explanation: NDCC 43-23-05.1(1)(c) requires the organization not to advertise or otherwise portray to the public that it is a real estate broker or brokerage firm. The statute does not require an unlicensed assistant, attorney ownership, or a separate trust account, and forming such an organization does not relieve the employing or associating broker of the duty to supervise.

question: An individual who forms a licensed organization under NDCC 43-23-05.1 while working as a salesperson, broker, or broker associate:
choice_a: Is not relieved of personal liability for licensed activities performed through the organization
choice_b: Is relieved of personal liability for the organization's licensed activities
choice_c: May thereafter operate without a supervising broker
choice_d: Automatically becomes the organization's designated broker
explanation: NDCC 43-23-05.1(3) expressly states that forming an organization does not, by nature of that act, relieve the individual of personal liability for licensed activities. Choice A states the opposite of the rule, and C and D are not supported by the statute, which also preserves the employing/associating broker's supervisory obligation under subsection 2.

question: What is the minimum age required to be licensed as either a real estate broker or a real estate salesperson in North Dakota?
explanation: NDCC 43-23-08(2) requires that, in addition to the general standards of subsection 1, an applicant for a broker's or salesperson's license must be at least eighteen years of age. The other ages are not the statutory minimum.

question: Before an applicant may be licensed as a North Dakota real estate broker, NDCC 43-23-08(3) generally requires the applicant to have:
choice_a: Completed a four-year college degree in business or real estate
choice_b: Served as a broker associate for at least one year
choice_c: Been actively engaged as a licensed real estate salesperson for at least two years preceding the application, or had substantially equal experience
choice_d: Personally closed at least ten real estate transactions
explanation: NDCC 43-23-08(3)(a)-(b) requires two years' active experience as a licensed salesperson immediately preceding application, or experience the commission determines to be substantially equal. No college degree, no minimum prior service as a broker associate, and no specific transaction count is required by statute.

question: Under NDCC 43-23-08(5), the commission may waive a broker applicant's two-year salesperson experience requirement because of area employment conditions. Which requirement may the commission NOT waive under this section?
choice_a: The examination fee
choice_b: The minimum age requirement
choice_c: The fingerprinting requirement
choice_d: The educational (prelicensing coursework) requirement
explanation: NDCC 43-23-08(5) expressly states that "the educational requirements of subsection 4 may not be waived by the commission," even though the experience requirement may be waived for area conditions. The other listed items are not addressed by this waiver provision.

question: How many hours of commission-approved prelicensing coursework must a North Dakota real estate salesperson applicant complete as a prerequisite for licensure?
choice_a: 90 hours
choice_b: 60 hours
choice_c: 75 hours
choice_d: 120 hours
explanation: NDCC 43-23-08(4) requires a salesperson applicant to furnish evidence of having "successfully completed at least ninety hours in courses of study approved by the commission." The other hour totals are not the statutory salesperson requirement.

question: In addition to the salesperson's prelicensing coursework, how many additional hours of commission-approved coursework must a North Dakota broker applicant complete under NDCC 43-23-08(4)?
choice_a: 30 additional hours
choice_b: 60 additional hours
choice_c: 45 additional hours
choice_d: 90 additional hours
explanation: NDCC 43-23-08(4) states: "An applicant for a broker's license must have successfully completed an additional sixty hours in courses of study approved by the commission," beyond the salesperson's ninety hours.

question: Under NDCC 43-23-08(4), may an applicant for a North Dakota salesperson's or broker's license sit for the licensing examination before completing the prerequisite prelicensing education?
choice_a: No, the education must be completed and proven before the exam may be taken
choice_b: Yes, and passing the exam waives the education requirement entirely
choice_c: Yes, but the commission may not issue the license until satisfactory evidence of completed education is furnished
choice_d: No, because North Dakota does not require any prelicensing education before licensure
explanation: The statute expressly permits an applicant to take the exam before fulfilling the educational prerequisite, but bars the commission from issuing a license until satisfactory evidence of completed education is furnished. A and D misstate the rule; C incorrectly claims passing the exam substitutes for the education requirement.

question: Which of the following activities, if performed for another for compensation, falls within North Dakota's statutory definition of acting as a "real estate broker" under NDCC 43-23-06.1(9)?
choice_a: Mowing the lawn of a vacant listed property as a maintenance contractor
choice_b: Providing a home inspection report to a buyer
choice_c: Appraising real property for a mortgage lender
choice_d: Negotiating or offering to negotiate the sale, exchange, purchase, or lease of real estate for another
explanation: NDCC 43-23-06.1(9)(d) lists negotiating or offering, attempting, or agreeing to negotiate a sale, exchange, purchase, or lease as one of the enumerated broker acts. Lawn maintenance, home inspection, and appraisal are separate occupations not within the real estate broker definition.

question: Under NDCC 43-23-07, which of the following persons is exempt from North Dakota's real estate broker or salesperson licensing requirement?
choice_a: An attorney at law admitted to practice in North Dakota handling a sale of real estate in the course of estate administration in district court
choice_b: A property management company employee handling third-party sales for a fee
choice_c: A licensed salesperson advertising listings on behalf of a broker
choice_d: A for-sale-by-owner seller who pays a flat referral fee to an unlicensed friend for finding a buyer
explanation: NDCC 43-23-07(1)(b) exempts an attorney admitted to practice in North Dakota who handles real estate sales in the course of estate or guardianship administration, trust administration, bankruptcy, or receivership actions subject to court approval. A is not exempt because it is fee-based third-party sales activity; C is a licensed activity, not an exemption from licensing; D would actually violate 43-23-11.1(1)(l), which prohibits paying compensation to an unlicensed person.

question: NDCC 43-23-07 exempts a person selling real estate as an auctioneer from real estate broker or salesperson licensure, but only if:
choice_a: The auctioneer is also a licensed salesperson in another state
choice_b: The sale is advertised as a bona fide public auction
choice_c: The auctioneer donates a portion of the commission to charity
choice_d: The property being auctioned is agricultural land only
explanation: NDCC 43-23-07(1)(c) conditions the auctioneer exemption on the sale being "advertised as a bona fide public auction." The other conditions are not part of the statutory exemption.

question: Under NDCC 43-23-10, when may the North Dakota Real Estate Commission recognize an out-of-state real estate broker's license as satisfying North Dakota's broker licensing qualifications?
choice_a: Only if the nonresident broker's home state has no licensing requirements
choice_b: Only if the nonresident broker relocates permanently to North Dakota within 90 days
choice_c: If the nonresident broker has qualified for a license as a broker in the broker's own state
choice_d: Only if North Dakota and the broker's home state have a formal written reciprocity treaty ratified by the legislature
explanation: NDCC 43-23-10 states the commission "shall recognize the license issued to a real estate broker by another state as satisfactorily qualifying the nonresident broker for license as a broker; provided, the nonresident broker has qualified for license in the broker's own state." No treaty or relocation requirement exists in the statute.

question: A nonresident broker seeking North Dakota licensure under NDCC 43-23-10's reciprocity provision must also file which document with the commission?
choice_a: A surety bond equal to one year's projected commissions
choice_b: A notarized letter of recommendation from the applicant's home-state broker
choice_c: Proof of North Dakota residency
choice_d: An irrevocable consent that suits and actions may be commenced against the applicant in North Dakota courts by service on the commission or executive director
explanation: NDCC 43-23-10 requires every nonresident applicant to file an irrevocable consent to service of process through the commission or executive director. A nonresident broker under this section is not required to maintain a place of business, or reside, in North Dakota, and no surety bond or letter of recommendation is required by this section.

question: According to the North Dakota Real Estate Commission's published application guidance, applicants already licensed in good standing at the same license level in which states may qualify for reciprocal North Dakota licensure without retaking the ND examination?
choice_a: Minnesota, Iowa, and Georgia
choice_b: South Dakota, Montana, and Wyoming
choice_c: Any state bordering North Dakota
choice_d: Any state that is also a PSI Services testing jurisdiction
explanation: NDREC's "How To Apply" guidance identifies Minnesota, Iowa, and Georgia as the states with which North Dakota has reciprocal recognition, allowing an applicant licensed and in good standing at the same level in one of those states to bypass the ND examination. The other choices do not reflect NDREC's published reciprocal states.

question: Under NDCC 43-23-13.1, how often must a person licensed as a North Dakota real estate broker or salesperson register (renew) with the commission?
choice_a: Every five years
choice_b: At a regular interval the commission sets, not less than annually
choice_c: Every two years
choice_d: Only once, upon initial licensure
explanation: NDCC 43-23-13.1(1) requires every licensed broker or salesperson to register "at a regular interval set by the commission not less than annually." The other choices misstate the renewal frequency.

question: Under NDCC 43-23-13.1, what happens to a North Dakota real estate license that is not renewed by the late renewal date set by the commission?
choice_a: It automatically converts to inactive status pending a hearing
choice_b: It remains valid for an additional 12-month grace period
choice_c: It is canceled without any notice or opportunity for a hearing, and the person must again satisfy the full application and examination requirements to become relicensed
choice_d: It is suspended until the licensee completes an ethics course
explanation: NDCC 43-23-13.1(1) provides that cancellation is performed without notice or opportunity for hearing, and a person whose license has been canceled must satisfy the application and examination requirements for prospective licensees to become relicensed. No automatic inactive status, grace period, or ethics-course cure is provided.

question: Under NDCC 43-23-08.2, what must an applicant for renewal of a North Dakota broker's or salesperson's license submit, beyond meeting the standards of 43-23-08?
choice_a: A new set of fingerprint cards for every renewal cycle
choice_b: A signed affidavit from the applicant's designated broker attesting to zero consumer complaints
choice_c: A copy of the applicant's federal tax return
choice_d: Proof of participation in commission-approved continuing education
explanation: NDCC 43-23-08.2(1) conditions renewal on submitting proof of participation in approved continuing education, with the required number of hours and reporting conditions set by the commission. Fingerprinting on every renewal, a zero-complaint affidavit, and tax returns are not renewal requirements under this section.

question: Under NDCC 43-23-08.2(3), which licensees are automatically exempt from North Dakota's continuing education renewal requirement?
choice_a: Licensees who had held a real estate license for fifteen continuous years as of January 1, 1984
choice_b: All broker associates, regardless of tenure
choice_c: Any licensee over the age of 65
choice_d: Licensees who completed prelicensing education within the last five years
explanation: NDCC 43-23-08.2(3) grandfathers licensees who held a real estate license continuously for fifteen years as of January 1, 1984. The commission may also grant discretionary exemptions for health, military service, or other good cause, but the automatic statutory exemption is the 1984 grandfather clause, not age or broker-associate status.

question: Under NDCC 43-23-12(2), if a licensed North Dakota real estate salesperson changes the broker under whom the salesperson is supervised, what must the salesperson do?
choice_a: Nothing, as long as the new broker separately notifies the commission
choice_b: Give the commission prompt written notice within five days of the change
choice_c: Retake the state portion of the licensing examination
choice_d: Complete an additional 30 hours of coursework before continuing to practice
explanation: NDCC 43-23-12(2) requires the salesperson to give the commission prompt written notice, within five days, of a change of broker and the name of the new supervising broker. Retaking the exam or completing extra coursework is not required for a broker change.

question: Under NDCC 43-23-12(2), what is the consequence if a licensed salesperson changes brokers without giving the required notice to the commission?
choice_a: The salesperson's license converts to broker-associate status
choice_b: The new broker is fined, but the salesperson's license remains valid
choice_c: The salesperson's license is automatically canceled
choice_d: The commission issues a warning letter, but the license remains active
explanation: The statute is explicit: "The change of broker by any licensed real estate salesperson, without notice to the commission, automatically cancels that person's license." The other outcomes are not provided for by the statute.

question: Under NDCC 43-23-12(2), once a real estate salesperson's supervision by a broker has been terminated, what is that salesperson prohibited from doing?
choice_a: Renewing an errors and omissions insurance policy
choice_b: Attending commission-approved continuing education courses
choice_c: Applying for reciprocal licensure in another state
choice_d: Performing any acts contemplated by NDCC chapter 43-23, directly or indirectly, until the commission reissues a license to a new broker
explanation: NDCC 43-23-12(2) makes it unlawful for a salesperson to perform any acts contemplated by chapter 43-23, directly or indirectly, after supervision by a broker has been terminated, until the license has been reissued by the commission to a new broker. The other options are not restricted by this provision.

question: Under NDCC 43-23-12(1), if a real estate broker removes the designated place of business, what must the broker do regarding the commission?
choice_a: Apply to the commission before the removal, or within five days after the removal, designating the new location
choice_b: Nothing is required unless the new location is outside the broker's home county
choice_c: Notify only the affected salespersons, not the commission
choice_d: Wait until the next annual renewal cycle to update the address
explanation: NDCC 43-23-12(1) requires the licensee to apply to the commission before removal, or within five days after removal, designating the new office location, after which the commission issues a new license for the unexpired period. The other choices misstate or omit this obligation.

question: Under NDCC 43-23-19, which North Dakota real estate licensees are required to carry errors and omissions (E&O) insurance as a condition of licensure?
choice_a: Only designated brokers
choice_b: All real estate salespersons and brokers, except those holding inactive licenses
choice_c: Only salespersons in their first year of licensure
choice_d: Only brokers who maintain a trust account
explanation: NDCC 43-23-19 requires E&O insurance of "all real estate salespersons and brokers, except those which hold inactive licenses." The requirement is not limited to designated brokers, first-year salespersons, or trust-account-holding brokers.

question: Under NDCC 43-23-08.1, does a criminal conviction automatically disqualify an applicant from North Dakota real estate licensure?
choice_a: Yes, any felony conviction is an automatic, permanent bar
choice_b: Yes, but only if the conviction occurred within North Dakota
choice_c: No, only if the commission determines the offense has a direct bearing on the person's ability to serve the public, or the person is not sufficiently rehabilitated
choice_d: No, criminal history is never considered in North Dakota real estate licensing
explanation: NDCC 43-23-08.1 provides that conviction of an offense does not disqualify a person from licensure unless the commission determines the offense has a direct bearing on the person's ability to serve the public as a broker or salesperson, or the person is not sufficiently rehabilitated under NDCC 12.1-33-02.1. A and C overstate an automatic bar, and D is wrong because criminal history is considered, including through the background checks authorized by 43-23-08.4.
